content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving sulfamethoxazole and various other medications. 1. Sulfamethoxazole can alter the metabolism of drugs processed by hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10, potentially increasing or decreasing their levels or effects. The clinical significance of some of these interactions is unknown. 2. Sulfamethoxazole and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Alternative drugs should be considered. 3. Sulfamethoxazole and iloperidone also prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring is recommended when co-administered. 4. Imatinib increases the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Sulfamethoxazole and imidapril may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia. Monitor potassium levels closely. 6. Sulfamethoxazole and imipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Additionally, sulfamethoxazole may decrease imipramine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is required. 7. Sulfamethoxazole and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval, and indapamide may increase sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. There is also a risk of hyponatremia. Alternative drugs or close monitoring is recommended. 8. Indomethacin may increase sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 9. Isocarboxazid may increase sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 10. Sulfamethoxazole and itraconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 11. Sulfamethoxazole and ketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Ketoconazole may also increase sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised. 12. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of L-methylfolate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 13. Sulfamethoxazole increases lacosamide levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Dose adjustment of lacosamide may be necessary when co-administered with strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 14. Sulfamethoxazole increases lamivudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 15. Sulfamethoxazole and lapatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Leflunomide increases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 17. Sulfamethoxazole increases lesinurad levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Sulfamethoxazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 19. Sulfamethoxazole and levoketoconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Levoketoconazole may also increase sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 20. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of oral contraceptives (levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate) by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Linezolid may increase sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 22. Sulfamethoxazole and lofepramine both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole may also decrease lofepramine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is required. 23. Sulfamethoxazole increases losartan levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism, potentially inhibiting the conversion of losartan to its active metabolite E-3174. The clinical significance is unknown, and individual therapeutic response should be monitored to adjust losartan dosage. 24. Sulfamethoxazole and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Sulfamethoxazole and maprotiline both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole may also decrease maprotiline levels through an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is advised. 26. Mefloquine increases the toxicity of sulfamethoxazole by prolonging the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 27. Sulfamethoxazole increases meloxicam levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 28. Sulfamethoxazole increases memantine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 29. Mesalamine increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Sulfamethoxazole increases metformin levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 32. Sulfamethoxazole and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 33. Methenamine and sulfamethoxazole may form an insoluble precipitate in the urine, reducing the effects of both agents. This combination is contraindicated. 34. Sulfamethoxazole increases the toxicity of methotrexate by competing for plasma protein binding, potentially elevating methotrexate concentrations and increasing the risk of toxicity (e.g., bone marrow suppression). This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 35. Methoxsalen and sulfamethoxazole may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to additive photosensitizing effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Metolazone increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. There is a risk of hyponatremia. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Sulfamethoxazole and metronidazole may decrease each other's metabolism. Metronidazole may also increase sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Miconazole (vaginal) increases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Sulfamethoxazole increases midodrine levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 40. Mineral oil decreases sulfamethoxazole levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 41. Mipomersen and sulfamethoxazole may increase each other's toxicity. Both drugs have the potential to elevate hepatic enzymes. Liver function tests (LFTs) should be monitored. 42. Sulfamethoxazole and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 43. Sulfamethoxazole increases nateglinide levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism and competing for plasma protein binding. Nateglinide may also increase sulfamethoxazole levels. The clinical significance is unknown, and close monitoring is advised. 44. Sulfamethoxazole and nilotinib both prolong the QTc interval. Nilotinib may also increase sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 45. Sulfamethoxazole and nitazoxanide may increase each other's levels through plasma protein binding competition. The clinical significance is unknown. 46. Sulfamethoxazole and nortriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole may also decrease nortriptyline levels through an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is required. 47. Sulfamethoxazole and octreotide both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 48. Sulfamethoxazole and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole may also increase ofloxacin levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown. 49. Sulfamethoxazole increases ospemifene levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism and competing for plasma protein binding. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 50. Sulfamethoxazole and paliperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 51. Sulfamethoxazole decreases pantothenic acid levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 52. Sulfamethoxazole increases parecoxib levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 53. Sulfamethoxazole and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 54. Sulfamethoxazole and pazopanib both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance is unknown. 55. Sulfamethoxazole and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 56. Pentobarbital decreases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 57. Sulfamethoxazole and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 58. Sulfamethoxazole and pexidartinib both inhibit gastrointestinal absorption. Pexidartinib can cause hepatotoxicity, and co-administration with other hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. 59. Phenelzine increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 60. Sulfamethoxazole increases phenindione effects by decreasing metabolism and competing for plasma protein binding. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 61. Phenobarbital decreases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 62. Sulfamethoxazole increases phenytoin levels by decreasing metabolism and affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 63. Sulfamethoxazole and pimozide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 64. Sulfamethoxazole increases piroxicam levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 65. Sulfamethoxazole and porfimer may synergistically enhance photosensitivity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 66. Sulfamethoxazole and posaconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 67. Sulfamethoxazole increases pralatrexate levels by decreasing renal clearance. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 68. Sulfamethoxazole and pretomanid may increase each other's toxicity. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity, and co-administration with hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. 69. Sulfamethoxazole and primaquine may synergistically increase the risk of hemolysis in patients with G6PD deficiency. The clinical significance is unknown. 70. Primidone decreases sulfamethoxazole levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 71. Probenecid increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 72. Sulfamethoxazole increases procainamide levels through competition for renal tubular clearance. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and this combination should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 73. Sulfamethoxazole and prochlorperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 74. Promazine increases sulfamethoxazole toxicity through an unspecified mechanism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 75. Sulfamethoxazole and promethazine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 76. Sulfamethoxazole increases protamine effects by decreasing metabolism and competing for plasma protein binding. This combination should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 77. Sulfamethoxazole and protriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole may also decrease protriptyline levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 78. Sulfamethoxazole decreases pyridoxine levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 79. Sulfamethoxazole decreases pyridoxine (antidote) levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown.
